title: Marketing Lead - B2B Demand Generation & Growth (m/w/d) - Remote
description: Über uns ZEP ist eine cloudbasierte Software für Projektcontrolling – von der Projektzeiterfassung über Abwesenheitsverwaltung bis zur Abrechnung. Mehr als 3.000 Unternehmen, vor allem projektorientierte Dienstleister wie Beratungen, IT- und Engineering-Unternehmen, arbeiten bereits mit ZEP. Seit unserer Gründung im Jahr 2000 sind wir inhabergeführt und kontinuierlich gewachsen. Jetzt wollen wir den nächsten Schritt gehen und noch mehr Unternehmen von ZEP überzeugen. Als Marketing Lead entwickelst du die passenden Ideen und Maßnahmen, um neue Kunden zu gewinnen und unser Wachstum aktiv voranzutreiben. Du willst Marketing nicht nur umsetzen, sondern verantworten – mit klaren Pipeline-Zielen, eigenem Budget und einem Team, das du weiterentwickelst? Als Marketing Lead bei ZEP übernimmst du die Ergebnisverantwortung für unser Marketing und die daraus entstehende Pipeline. Du führst das Marketingteam sowie unsere Agenturen und Dienstleister, steuerst das Marketingbudget und greifst aktiv ein, wenn Zahlen vom Plan abweichen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit Sales und der Geschäftsführung zusammen. Du verbindest strategisches Denken mit einer Hands-on-Mentalität dort, wo es darauf ankommt. Deine Aufgaben Du verantwortest unsere Pipeline-Ziele und das Marketingbudget und steuerst aktiv gegen, wenn Zahlen abweichen. Du entwickelst die Marketingstrategie gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung, schärfst Positionierung und Messaging für unsere B2B-Zielgruppen und leitest daraus Ziele und Prioritäten ab. Als Teil des Management-Teams bringst du die Marketingperspektive in strategische Entscheidungen auf Unternehmensebene ein und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung von ZEP aktiv mit. Du führst das Marketingteam, setzt Prioritäten und entwickelst die Teammitglieder fachlich und persönlich weiter. Du steuerst und forderst unsere Agenturen und Dienstleister – insbesondere im Paid-Bereich (z. B. Google Ads, Paid Social) – mit klaren Zielen und Briefings und misst sie an ihren Ergebnissen. Du baust Demand Generation über mehrere Kanäle auf, nicht nur über Paid. Du verbesserst gemeinsam mit dem Vertrieb die Lead-Qualität und die Übergabe an Sales. Du sorgst für sauberes Tracking und Attribution über den gesamten Funnel. Du wertest Kampagnen, Funnel und Conversion Rates aus – wenn nötig selbst in HubSpot und im Tracking – und leitest daraus konkrete nächste Schritte ab. Du entwickelst SEO und die Sichtbarkeit in KI-Suchen (AI Search) als wachsenden Kanal weiter. Du entwickelst unsere Website weiter und holst mehr Leads aus dem vorhandenen Traffic. Deine Voraussetzungen Du bringst mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-SaaS-Marketing mit, mit Schwerpunkt Demand Generation. Du hast nachweislich Pipeline- oder Umsatzziele erreicht und hattest Budgetverantwortung. Du hast bereits Führungserfahrung gesammelt: Du hast ein Marketingteam geführt, Prioritäten gesetzt und Mitarbeitende weiterentwickelt. Du hast Erfahrung darin, Agenturen und Dienstleister zu steuern und fachlich zu fordern. Du kennst dich mit Performance Marketing (Google Ads, Paid Social) so gut aus, dass du Agenturen auf Augenhöhe führst. Du bist sicher in Analyse, Tracking und Attribution; idealerweise hast du Erfahrung mit HubSpot. Du setzt KI selbstverständlich in deiner Arbeit ein und weißt, wo sie echten Mehrwert bringt. Du bringst eine Hands-on-Mentalität mit und wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jeder nächste Schritt vorgegeben wird. Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und kannst dich auch auf Englisch sicher verständigen. Deine Benefits 30 Tage Urlaub und unbefristete Arbeitsverträge Remote First Company – Arbeite innerhalb Deutschlands von wo du möchtest! Unterstützung bei der Home-Office Einrichtung Chancen, Freiheiten und Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten eines Startups verbunden mit der Sicherheit eines seit über 20 Jahren etablierten Unternehmens im Mittelstand. Flexible Arbeitszeiten – Keine Kernarbeitszeiten, stimme dich einfach mit dem Team ab. Windows oder Mac? Entscheide selbst! 50 EUR monatlicher Gutschein für verschiedene Sachbezüge oder Urban Sports Mitgliedschaft Jobrad mit Arbeitgeber-Zuschuss offene team- und ergebnisorientierte Kultur regelmäßige Workshops, Mittagessen und Events zum Teambuilding Individuelle Altersvorsorgepläne Wenn du dich in den Anforderungen wiederfindest und diesen Bereich aktiv mitgestalten möchtest, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung! title: Manager: Compliance Advisory (and Data Protection)
location: London or remote within the UK
description: About Griffin Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences. We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more. We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies. Learn more about what we do Our culture We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible. We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life. We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified. Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers. Learn more about our culture. The Team You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow. The opportunity We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end. As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into. Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it. What success looks like In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation. Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand. To do this you'll be involved in: Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time) Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start. Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures. Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material. Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged. Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use. Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time. Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes. Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge. Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed) Being our DPO means: advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs) monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data. We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are. Your background We need a proactive compliance doer first and foremost. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there. To ensure this, we're looking for people who have: Compliance experience in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm. Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products , like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting. Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements for product, sales or operations teams. An openness to picking up data protection as part of the role: a genuine interest is enough, DPO experience isn’t required. A curious, questioning approach. You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against. The confidence to challenge, clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right. A love of writing . We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write ). Ideally, you would also: Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area, such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar. Have been a DPO, or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm. Have worked in finance or banking. What can we offer you? We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future. Salary: £ 80-90 (DOE) Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year) Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment. As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks How long will the process take? We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other. Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience. Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements. Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin. Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview. Step 5 : Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here . How do I apply? Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next. We’re remote-first We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. What matters is the work, not where you do it. Under representation At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance Griffin Bank Ltd request that recruitment agencies do not speculatively submit CVs to any employee or associate of our company unless explicitly asked to do so by a member of our Talent team. Any CVs sent to any member of our team on a speculative basis will not be recognised and we will not accept liability for any fee or commission should we subsequently employ a candidate who applied to us directly or was introduced by an instructed agency that may also have been submitted speculatively by an uninstructed agency. title: B2B Sponsorship Sales Executive
location: Hybrid, or Fully Remote within the UK
description: About The Alliance When it comes to building world-class professional communities, The Alliance is leading the way. From Product Marketing and Sales Enablement to Product-Led Growth, AI, Customer Success, and CMOs, we're home to some of the most engaged and influential communities in the industry. With 160,000+ professionals across our communities and a constant stream of content, courses, events, and memberships, we help our members learn, connect, and grow. Our executive events are a key part of that mission—bringing together senior leaders to share insights, tackle industry challenges, and build meaningful relationships. Every year, we engage attendees, speakers, partners, and members from some of the world's leading organisations and fastest-growing start-ups, including TikTok, Microsoft, Peloton, and Uber . About the Role We’re looking for an ambitious, commercially driven B2B Sales Executive to join our Sponsorship Sales team at The Alliance. Ideally, you’ll have experience in B2B sales, events, media, or delegate sales, and be comfortable working towards ambitious targets and KPIs. You’ll already understand the importance of prospecting, building relationships, and closing deals, and now you’re ready to develop those skills further in a new commercial environment. At The Alliance, we connect leading B2B brands with senior decision-makers through our professional communities, exclusive events, and tailored sponsorship solutions. You’ll have the opportunity to work with established brands, develop your commercial expertise, and learn how to sell higher-value solutions. We’re looking for someone who wants more than just their next sales job. Someone who is motivated to improve, ready to take ownership of their results, and determined to build a successful long-term career in sales. Sponsorship products: Sponsored Digital Products: (i.e webinars, reports and lead generation campaigns): Scalable, bespoke programs that connect vendors with our communities through awareness and lead generation. Face-to-Face Events: Summits sponsorships, from an expo table to becoming part of the event itself. These give sponsors direct, in-person access to our community, from meeting attendees at their stand to being part of the event experience, with the chance to build relationships. What You Will Be Doing New Business Development: Proactively identify and approach prospective clients to generate new business opportunities. Prospecting & Outreach: Build a strong pipeline through outbound calls, emails, research, and consistent follow-up. Building Relationships: Develop relationships with prospective clients, understand their needs, and identify commercial opportunities. Sales & Negotiation: Present relevant solutions, handle objections, negotiate effectively, and close deals. Revenue Generation: Work towards ambitious sales targets and KPIs, taking ownership of your performance and results. Pipeline Management: Maintain accurate sales records, track opportunities, and manage your pipeline effectively. Account Development: Identify opportunities to grow existing client relationships and generate repeat business. Continuous Improvement: Learn from experienced colleagues, act on feedback, and continuously develop your sales skills. What We’re Looking For Sales Experience: Ideally, experience in B2B sales, delegate sales, events, media, or another target-driven commercial environment. A Proven Sales Mindset: You’re comfortable working towards demanding targets and KPIs and motivated by achieving results. Confidence & Communication: You can build rapport, engage prospects, and communicate commercial value effectively. A Hunter Mentality: You enjoy prospecting, opening doors, generating opportunities, and winning new business. Resilience & Determination: You can handle rejection, stay focused under pressure, and maintain momentum. Commercial Ambition: You want to develop your sales ability, take on greater responsibility, and increase your earning potential as you progress. A Desire to Learn: You’re receptive to coaching, willing to challenge yourself, and committed to continuous improvement. Above all, we want people who are hungry to succeed, take pride in their results, and are serious about taking their sales career to the next level. If you have the drive to deliver results and the ambition to become an exceptional salesperson, we’d love to hear from you. Location: This role can be either Hybrid in our London office or completely remote across the UK (not abroad). Salary: Base Salary range £32K - £38K (*Based on previous experience) - OTE £60K+ _______________________ Benefits Time off & flexibility 34 days’ paid holiday including UK Bank holidays and a day off on your birthday Flexible working hours : our core hours are 10am–4:30pm, with the flexibility to structure your working day between 8am and 8pm around when you work best Work from where works for you : choose to work remotely within the UK or hybrid from our London office. Our office is always open to the wider team whenever you fancy coming in WFH Kit: a comprehensive tech setup, plus a dedicated WFH equipment budget A well-stocked office : snacks, drinks and fresh fruit available in our London office Health & wellbeing Private Medical and Dental Insurance with Bupa Life Insurance: cover worth 4x your annual salary On-demand therapy & coaching : company sponsored access to therapy and career coaching through Spill Wellness perks : discounts on gym memberships, fitness and wellness classes Cycle to Work & Workplace Nursery schemes Perks at Work : access to a wide range of corporate discounts Monthly flexible benefits allowance through ThanksBen (£50/month in year one, £100/month in year two and £165/month from year three), giving you extra flexibility to spend on the benefits that matter most to you Learning & development A growing personal L&D budget (starting at £500 per year and increasing with tenure to £3,000 per year) Dedicated L&D or volunteering time : one paid day every quarter to invest in your development or support a cause you care about. Unlimited access to our internal Academy : including courses, learning resources and professional certifications Community and Inclusion We are committed to creating a workplace that is free from discrimination and bias, and where everyone has equal opportunities to succeed and contribute. We acknowledge that our work here is never done - and we promise to continue striving for inclusivity every day. If you’re worried you don’t quite hit all the requirements we’ve listed, don’t let that hold you back from submitting your application! Unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are essential for our ability to innovate and grow, so if you think you’d be a great fit then we’d love to hear from you. We are The Alliance - in more ways than one. title: Manager, Assigned Support Engineering (EMEA)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><div class="section page-centered"> <div class="section page-centered"> <p><strong>What this role is about</strong></p> <p>You'll manage a team of Assigned Support Engineers who provide relationship-based technical support to GitLab's biggest enterprise customers. ASEs work proactively with customers to find root causes and prevent repeat issues, which is different from working a ticket queue. They also turn their actions and activity into outcomes and deliverables that show customers the ROI they get from GitLab.</p> <p>You'll build a team that works independently, owns issues from start to finish, and knows when to ask for help. When a customer relationship is in trouble, you'll work alongside the account teams to bring it back to health. You'll also help improve the ASE program in ways that matter to customers and to the company.</p> <p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hire, coach, and develop ASEs. Hold regular 1:1s, give direct feedback, deal with performance issues early, and build a team where people feel safe raising problems.</li> <li>Pay attention to engagement and retention, and coach the team on GitLab's values and operating principles.</li> <li>Train ASEs to run technical interviews so the hiring pipeline doesn't depend on you.</li> <li>Set clear goals and expectations, track progress across onboarding, relationships, escalations, and KPIs, and connect the team's work to company priorities. Help ASEs prioritize across accounts when everything feels urgent.</li> <li>Lead escalations from start to finish. Work with Engineering, Product, Sales, and Customer Success to get the right people moving, and keep the customer informed and confident in the plan.</li> <li>Work alongside the account teams to bring at-risk customers back to health, including renewal and expansion risk driven by support concerns. Build the recovery plan, drive the technical side, and report on progress until the customer is stable.</li> <li>Help ASEs translate their actions and activity into outcomes, deliverables, and ROI, and present that to customers and executives in clear decks that cover what happened, what you're doing about it, and what comes next.</li> <li>Work with the ASE leadership team on initiatives that improve the program and customer outcomes, and see yours through to results.</li> <li>Partner with Sales, Customer Success, CSMs, Product, and Engineering to push for what customers need, and contribute utilization and onboarding data to capacity and headcount planning with Finance and sales leadership.</li> <li>Document how the team works and find ways to make it more efficient through tools, process changes, and automation. Use AI well in your own work and coach ASEs to do the same.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you'll bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years in technical support, with at least 2 years managing customer-facing technical teams.</li> <li>Experience with high-touch or assigned support for enterprise customers. Professional services delivery counts. Experience across Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com is a plus.</li> <li>A strong record of handling escalations with both internal teams and customers. You stay calm, keep people aligned, and know when to bring in leadership.</li> <li>The ability to turn a complicated or nuanced situation into a clear written story and tie activity to outcomes with numbers.</li> <li>A customer-centric approach balanced with good judgment about what the service, the team, and the company can deliver, and experience working with account teams to bring struggling customers back to health.</li> <li>A record of getting work done across teams through influence and strong working relationships. You can work with Sales, CS, and account teams to set clear expectations for the ASE service and find the right path for each customer.</li> <li>Willingness to be available outside standard hours, including weekends, for the occasional critical escalation or customer-impacting incident.</li> <li>Comfort with ambiguity and change. You keep a team steady while priorities, processes, and the program evolve, and you explain the reasons for changes so people stay engaged.</li> <li>A strong technical foundation to guide engineers in complex, production-critical environments, including Linux system administration and web application development concepts. Familiarity with Git, DevOps practices, or GitLab is helpful.</li> <li>A history of developing engineers at different skill levels through real feedback, mentoring, and clear expectations.</li> <li>Process skills that make a team more efficient without adding bureaucracy, and comfort leading a remote, globally distributed team using metrics and customer feedback.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The ASE team is spread across AMER, EMEA, and APAC and works mostly async, with regular pairing sessions, 1:1s, and Slack. We support GitLab's largest and most strategic customers, who run GitLab in production-critical environments. We dig into code and logs, work across departments, and focus on root cause, trends, preventing repeat issues, and providing the technical acumen that helps customers get the most value out of GitLab for their business.</p> </div> </div><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. title: Director of Global Training
description: UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable. Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia. UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems. About the Role As Director of Global Training, you’ll shape UFORCE’s global training capability, enabling customers to operate our uncrewed systems safely, legally and effectively. Reporting to the VP Military Exercises, you’ll set a consistent standard across markets, working through training schools, regional and technical teams while local delivery and commercial ownership remain with the regions. What You Will Do Own global operator and maintainer syllabi, assessment and certification, with controlled materials, consistent thresholds and appropriate local adaptation. Develop training for new products and command-and-control systems, including individual and group operation, communications and configuration. Turn validated field experience, including lessons from Ukraine and exercises, into practical instruction within security and sharing restrictions. Assure standards through school visits, authorisation and certification records, near-miss reporting and corrective actions, feeding findings into training improvements and VP-led safety investigations. Lead the UK-first route to training-authority recognition with Legal and country leads, distinguishing operating permissions from authority to train and certify and using third-party provision where needed. Set common course pricing and align instructors and assets with confirmed demand. Coordinate customer-site training with clear responsibilities for safety, equipment and field engineer support. Build a sustainable in-house instructor capability, supported by external providers for specialist needs and peak demand. Deliver cost-effective simulation and blended learning, building on existing capability, managing the allocated budget and retaining hands-on training where essential. What We're Looking For Multi-site training leadership in defence, military or a comparable safety-critical technical environment, with hands-on experience in course design, assessment and instructor standardisation. Credibility with experienced operators and instructors, sound security judgement and a track record of improving training through operational feedback. Strong cross-functional leadership, with the ability to secure commitments and resolve resource conflicts without direct line authority. Experience contributing to regulatory approvals or audits, alongside training pricing and capacity planning. Experience delivering simulation or blended-learning programmes, with sound budget and learning-outcome decisions. An inclusive, accountable leadership style that encourages honest reporting and protects safety and standards under pressure. Willingness to travel regularly to training bases, customer sites and exercises. Nice to Have Operational experience with uncrewed systems, including frontline or conflict-environment experience, or training experience in command and control. Experience with training-authority processes and international operating permissions. Experience delivering training in multiple languages and adapting it for different cultures. Experience building an internal instructor pipeline. Familiarity with security clearance constraints that affect who can deliver training. The nature of combat has changed. Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability. And UFORCE is ready. Are You? Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Portfolio analytics and forecasts actuary
description: Health can’t wait . Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. ⭐️ The Insurance Team ⭐️ Being part of Alan's insurance community is a great opportunity to have a significant impact on people's health and wellbeing in our multiple countries of operation. We are at the heart of Alan’s mission , bringing to the team our technical leadership and expertise on healthcare and death & disability insurance. title: Senior Product Manager, Data Products
description: ABOUT THE TEAM When the world's largest organizations bet on Mural , Govern & Trust is the team that earns that trust at scale. We build the experiences that help enterprises roll out Mural with confidence, keep it secure, and see the impact it has on how their people work. Data sits at the center of it all. Admins are Mural's most demanding data consumers: they need to prove ROI to their leadership, guide adoption across thousands of people, and account for every action. If data products can meet their bar, they'll work for everyone. Mural has a modern data platform, strong data engineering and analytics teams, and a wealth of data on how teams collaborate. The next step is treating that data as a product in its own right, with a dedicated owner for what it means and how it's used. YOUR MISSION As a Senior Product Manager you'll define the metrics that describe how Mural creates value, and make them the shared foundation for everything built on top. The same definitions will power internal product decisions, the Insights experience Admins use in the product, and the reporting API and MCP server that customers and AI agents query. This role starts upstream. You'll work from raw product events to decide what each metric should measure, how it's calculated, and what the data needs to look like for customers and internal teams to rely on it. Then you'll turn those metrics into experiences that help organizations understand and grow their use of Mural. WHAT YOU'LL DO The evolution of data products. Shape how Mural's data products move from reporting on what happened to guiding what happens next. Work across the Govern & Trust portfolio to define how insights become part of how organizations run Mural. The metric layer. Define Mural's shared, cross-product metrics, like activity, collaboration, and adoption. Set the standards that let product teams define and publish their own metrics consistently. Data Engineering builds and runs the layer; you shape what goes in it and how it evolves. Internal product analytics. Be a thought partner to domain PMs as they set their north-star metrics, and make product data easy for them to explore on their own. Work with Business Analytics to keep product-facing and business-facing reporting working together. Customer-facing data products. Own the strategy and roadmap for Insights: in-product reporting and dashboards, exports and APIs, audit logs, and the methodology behind every number customers see. AI and agent access. Package and launch Mural's customer-facing reporting MCP server: which data it exposes, which plans get it, and what guardrails apply. Define how natural-language and agent-driven analysis extends Insights. Instrumentation. R&D teams own emitting events. Your job is to raise the bar on what they emit. Set per-product requirements for granularity and retention, which differ for audit logs, activity data, and product analytics. Partner with Data Engineering on event standards so metrics start from good data. WHAT YOU'LL BRING 5+ years of product management experience, including shipping at least one analytics or reporting product used by paying business customers. You defined the metrics behind it, not just the UI. A track record of making messy or conflicting data trustworthy: reconciling competing definitions, writing metric specs engineers could build from, and getting instrumentation changed upstream. Experience building both platform products, where your customers are internal teams or developers, and end-user-facing data products like analytics, reporting, or insights. You understand how the two have to work together. Working knowledge of modern data stacks: event pipelines, warehouses and lakehouses, dbt-style modeling, and semantic layers. You can write SQL and pull data yourself. The ability to get agreement on definitions across teams you don't manage, including PMs, data engineering, analytics, finance, and go-to-market. Experience with enterprise admin or governance products (IAM, security, compliance, audit) Hands-on experience with semantic layer tools (dbt Semantic Layer, Cube, LookML) Experience designing APIs, MCP servers, or connectors for analytics Equal Opportunity We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. title: Channel Account Manager
description: About Ping Identity : At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it. Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear. While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work. We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management. The Channel Account Manager (CAM) at Ping Identity plays a vital role in supporting the growth and success of the company's channel and alliances GTM. This role involves collaborating with the Partner ecosystem to develop and manage partnerships, help drive joint business development initiatives, and ensure effective communication and coordination with our channel partners. The CAM will contribute to the expansion of Ping Identity's market reach and the achievement of revenue goals. Reporting into the VP of Partnerships APJ, you will manage and support target partners across all Partner tiers helping to manage our partners across Australia and New Zealand. Work closely with the sales team across Australia and New Zealand to support their regional GTM requirements Important - You will ensure the Ping sales team are able to focus on finding, qualifying and closing opportunities with our partners - you act as the conduit between our sales team and our partners Support and drive the development of joint value propositions with our partners. Collaborate with partners to execute partner agreements and ensure other agreements are in place as required. Assist in driving partner enablement, including the development of sales practices and training programs. Help partners with deal registrations, portal access, program benefits etc. Contribute to tracking partner performance against agreed-upon metrics, such as revenue targets and pipeline development. Foster collaborative relationships with partners through ongoing engagement, communication, and business reviews. Support the execution of marketing and demand generation activities with partners to drive brand awareness and lead generation. Support the promotion and engagement with the Ping Partner program and related tools and processes. Assist in coordinating and participating in joint business planning activities with partners. Collaborate with internal teams to ensure effective communication and coordination with partners. Assist in ensuring partner success by monitoring delivery quality, customer satisfaction, and support. Contribute to joint pursuits with partners, identifying and developing sales opportunities and impacting existing opportunities to close with the influence of Partners. Stay updated on industry trends, market dynamics, and competitor activities to identify new business opportunities and challenges Required Skills & Qualifications: This role is based in Sydney or Melbourne. Important - This role requires regular collaboration with Ping colleagues and partners, typically including multiple in-person meetings each week. Additional partner or customer meetings may be required as the business needs dictate. You have 3+ year’s experience managing partners and exposure to GSI & Advisory Partners would be a bonus. Alternatively, you have excelled in a Partner BDR/SDR function and are looking to move up in your career. You have a good understanding of the Australia and New Zealand market. You are currently working in the SaaS industry, but working in Cyber Security and SaaSwill move you right to the top of the list. Understanding of channel sales strategies and partner ecosystems. Ability to drive mutual business outcomes for both Ping and our Partners - this includes regular cadence, partner QBRs etc. Good CRM opportunity hygiene (Salesforce preferred). Strong organisational and coordination skills and the ability to work cross functionally with presales, marketing, professional services, customer success etc. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. Willingness to learn and adapt to changing priorities and responsibilities. Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced environment. Ability to travel domestically as required and 1-2 international trips per year (US). …and have fun and enjoy the ride working in a very high growth dynamic environment for a great company headquartered in Denver Colorado Other: Familiarity with Salesforce.com or other CRM systems. Previous experience or exposure to channel sales, alliances management, or partner enablement is a must. Interest in the software industry and identity access management sector. Knowledge of marketing and demand generation practices. Understanding of partner training and sales enablement processes. Ability to analyse data and generate insights to drive partner performance. Proactive and positive mindset with a focus on continuous improvement. Life at Ping: We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day. Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special: A company culture that empowers you to do your best work. Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone. Regular company and team bonding events. Competitive benefits and perks. Global volunteering and community initiatives Our Benefits: Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule Parental Leave Progressive Healthcare Options Retirement Programs Opportunity for Education Reimbursement Commuter Offset (Specific locations) Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone’s individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self. We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

title: Staffing Associate (Contract)
description: About Invisible Invisible Technologies makes AI work. Our end-to-end AI platform structures messy data, automates digital workflows, deploys agentic solutions, measures outcomes, and integrates human expertise where it matters most. Our platform cleans, labels, and structures company data so it is ready for AI. It adapts models to each business and adds human expertise when needed, the same approach we have used to improve models for more than 80% of the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, AWS, and Cohere. Our successes span industries, from supply chain automation for Swiss Gear to AI-enabled naval simulations with SAIC, and validating NBA draft picks for the Charlotte Hornets. Profitable for more than half a decade, Invisible reached $134M in revenue and ranked as the number two fastest growing AI company on the 2024 Inc. 5000. In September 2025, we raised $100M in growth capital to accelerate our mission of making AI actually work in the enterprise and to advance our platform technology. About The Role The Staffing Associate at Invisible Technologies gets qualified experts onto client projects and billing fast. Working with the Sr. Manager, Staffing, you'll turn client demand into staffed, productive teams: sourcing and vetting contractors, matching them to the right engagement, and moving them through onboarding to their first billed client hour. Demand shifts quickly, and projects often need to be staffed in days, not weeks. This is a 6-month, 40-hour-per-week contract with real potential to extend or convert. It suits a seasoned, agency-trained staffing professional who measures success in fill rates and billed hours, thrives on urgency, and wants to make an immediate impact. What You’ll Do Staff client projects end to end, turning incoming client demand into qualified contractors who are onboarded and billing hours. Partner with delivery and operations leads to understand each project's skill, volume and timeline needs, then build a staffing plan to meet them. Source high volumes of contractors and subject-matter experts through LinkedIn Recruiter, job boards, referrals, talent communities and existing talent pools. Screen and vet candidates quickly against project requirements, including skills assessments where needed. Match and assign contractors to the right engagements, balancing skills, availability and client priorities. Move contractors from offer through contracting, onboarding and training to their first billed hour, clearing blockers along the way. Track every contractor's path to billing and follow up quickly with anyone who stalls between acceptance and active work. Redeploy contractors as projects ramp up, wind down or change scope to keep utilization high. Re-prioritize daily as urgent client needs open, working alongside the Sr. Manager, Staffing. Keep the ATS and staffing trackers accurate and report weekly on fill rate, time-to-staff, time-to-first-billed-hour and utilization. What We Need 5+ years of recruiting or staffing experience, including meaningful time in a staffing agency with a track record of meeting fill, placement and billable-hours targets. Proven success in high-volume contract or contingent staffing, filling dozens of seats at once while keeping quality high. A strong sense of urgency: you're energized by tight deadlines and can get qualified contractors from first contact to working in days. Advanced sourcing skills, including Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter and creative channels for niche or hard-to-find skills. Experience managing contractor onboarding, including contracts, compliance and readiness, in partnership with operations teams. Comfort working directly with delivery teams and client stakeholders, and pushing back when needed to keep staffing on track. Hands-on expertise with an ATS or staffing system (e.g., Greenhouse, Bullhorn, Workday, iCIMS) and strong spreadsheet skills for tracking pipelines. Sound judgment with confidential candidate, rate and client information. What’s In It For You Invisible is committed to fair and competitive pay for our contractors, ensuring that rates reflect both market conditions and the value each contractor brings. Our contractor rate structure accounts for regional differences in cost of living. As a contractor, you will not be eligible for Invisible’s employee benefits, bonus, or equity programs. Final rates are determined by a combination of factors, including location, job-related experience, skills, knowledge, and overall market conditions. Additional details on rate, contract duration, and terms will be discussed during the hiring process. You can find more information about our geographic pay tiers here . During the interview process, your Invisible Talent Acquisition Partner will confirm which tier applies to your location. For candidates outside the U.S., compensation is adjusted to reflect local market conditions and cost of living. *Bonuses and equity are included in all full-time offers. Final compensation is determined by a combination of factors, including location, job-related experience, skills, knowledge, internal pay equity, and overall market conditions. Because of this, every offer is unique. Additional details on total compensation and benefits will be discussed during the hiring process. What It's Like to Work at Invisible: At Invisible, we’re not just redefining work—we’re reinventing it. We operate at the intersection of advanced AI and human ingenuity, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible to unlock productivity and scale. Ownership is at the core of everything we do. Here, you won’t just execute tasks—you’ll build, innovate, and shape the future alongside world-class clients pushing the boundaries of AI. We expect bold ideas, relentless drive, and the ability to turn ambiguity into opportunity. The pace is fast, the challenges are big, and the growth is unmatched. We’re not for everyone, and we’re okay with that. If you’re looking for predictable routines, this isn’t the place for you. But if you’re driven to create, thrive in dynamic environments, and want a front-row seat to the AI revolution, you’ll fit right in. Country Hiring Guidelines: Invisible is a hybrid organization with offices and team members located around the world. While some roles may offer remote flexibility, most positions involve in-office collaboration and are tied to specific locations. Any location-based requirements or hybrid expectations will be communicated by our Talent Acquisition team during the recruiting process. AI Interviewing Guidelines: Our hiring team thoughtfully uses AI to support an efficient, engaging, and inclusive interview process. Since AI can also be a helpful tool for candidates, we've outlined expectations for using it ethically throughout your interview journey. Click here to learn more about how we use AI and our guidelines for candidates. Accessibility Statement: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities. If you require an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please submit your request using our accommodation request form. A member of our team will follow up to support your request. Here is the link the google form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScqsu0PCQ0m0lwt-VFeXovNbZxWk0jogv8QI_ciGqZsIbSBjQ/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=102356854798492362557 Equal Opportunity Statement: We’re an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. Due to a high volume of candidates, Invisible may use automated decision-maker technologies to filter candidates based on response to our application questions and other provided information. Our use of automated decision-making enables us to be efficient by providing a manageable list of possible candidates that meet our mandatory hiring criteria. title: Business Process Lead, Order to Cash
description: About Kaseya Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success. Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide. Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in. At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it. Position Summary The Business Process Lead, Order to Cash owns the end-to-end design of the business processes that run from order acceptance through cash collection and recognized revenue. This role is the connective tissue between the business stakeholders who operate these processes and the technology teams that build supporting systems, and is accountable for the detailed capability decomposition of this value stream. Process design decisions in this role have direct consequences for billing accuracy, revenue recognition, and financial reporting integrity, and the role carries a corresponding financial control responsibility. Importantly, this role owns the business capabilities in this value stream — their definition, design, decomposition, and governance — in close partnership with the business teams that operate the underlying functions day to day. It does not own those functions themselves; success depends on heavy partnership with business and technology leads rather than on direct authority. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role: the person hired personally facilitates working sessions, maps processes, writes requirements, and stays engaged through delivery and adoption. It also sits within a newly created function whose operating model and standards are still being defined, giving the person hired real influence over how the broader practice takes shape. The role holds several formal agreements with peer process owners covering shared boundaries, and maintaining those agreements is a core, ongoing part of the job rather than an occasional task. Key Responsibilities Own and continuously maintain a detailed (L2/L3) decomposition of order and subscription management, software provisioning and fulfillment, usage consumption and rating, billing and invoicing, invoice-to-cash, and revenue recognition capabilities, keeping documentation accurate as the operating model and systems landscape evolve, and using standards shared across the Business Process Lead team. Facilitate structured working sessions with business stakeholders across this value stream to document how processes work today and design how they should work going forward, producing process maps, documented decisions, and requirements a technical team can act on without extensive follow-up. Translate future-state process designs into system requirements, partner with Product Owners and Engineering Leads through design, build, and testing, and confirm that what gets delivered reflects the intended process design. Support two parallel delivery tracks — current, in-production systems and the next-generation platform build — correctly identifying which track an incoming request belongs to, and ensuring lessons learned in day-to-day operations are reflected back into documentation and forward-looking design work. Own change management, enablement, and adoption for process changes in this value stream — stakeholder impact assessment, readiness planning, training materials, and post-launch verification that new processes are being used as intended — and define and report the process performance metrics that show whether they are working. Hold and maintain documented agreements at shared boundaries with peer Business Process Leads, so handoffs between value streams are explicitly agreed rather than assumed. Own the capability design for software provisioning and fulfillment — manual provisioning, provisioning error handling, feature enablement, software suspension and reinstatement, and trial extension — partnering with the teams who operate those processes. Own the capability design for usage consumption and rating, including overage management and how rated usage flows into billing and revenue treatment. Required Qualifications Working knowledge of revenue recognition standards (ASC 606) and subscription billing mechanics, with the demonstrated ability to reason independently through how a mid-contract order change flows to invoicing, revenue schedules, and unbilled or deferred revenue balances. This is a firm screening requirement given the financial control responsibilities of the role, not a general preference. 5+ years of experience in business process design, business analysis, business architecture, or operations in a relevant domain. Demonstrated experience decomposing business capabilities into detailed, multi-level structures. Strong facilitation skills with cross-functional business stakeholders, including experience working at a director level, and comfort holding formal cross-functional agreements with peer process owners rather than treating a boundary handoff as a one-time conversation. Experience translating business process requirements into system requirements or work items for a technical delivery team, along with strong documentation habits. Preferred Qualifications Experience with contract modification accounting and its process implications in a subscription business. Billing operations, collections, or revenue accounting process design experience. Experience with consumption or usage-based billing and rating models, including how overages are handled and billed. Experience with software provisioning, license entitlement, or feature enablement process ownership. Indirect tax process design experience, including taxability determination, nexus, and exemption certificate management. Prior experience partnering with a shared platform engineering team on roadmap sequencing and prioritization. Experience with Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced, a dedicated revenue recognition engine such as RightRev, Oracle and NetSuite, and indirect tax engines such as OneSource or CertifyTax. #IND525 Additional information Kaseya provides equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, age, ancestry, gender, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Manager, Product Design, Growth (Upper Funnel)
description: ABOUT THE TEAM At Mural , we’re reimagining how teams think and create together. The Design and Research team brings clarity to complexity, shaping experiences that help people collaborate, ideate, and solve problems visually. We partner deeply with engineering, product, and research to invent the next generation of collaborative work combining craft, systems thinking, and bold exploration. YOUR MISSION As a Lead Product Designer focused on Growth, you’ll define how Mural earns user trust at the moments that matter most when someone first encounters the product's value, decides to go deeper, or chooses to stay. This is end to end growth journey ownership. It's about designing the logic of how Mural grows: the moments where clarity converts, where friction is a design failure, and where the line between growth and product quality either holds or breaks. You'll work across discovery, activation, and pricing surfaces, onboarding paths, upgrade flows, lifecycle touchpoints, and in-product nudges. Most importantly, you'll orchestrate how those surfaces work together and set the standard for how growth design is practiced at Mural. You'll succeed if you can bring full journey thinking, rigor and craft to a domain that often defaults to shortcuts and if you can help a cross-functional team understand what good growth design actually looks like. WHAT YOU'LL DO Player Responsibilities (Individual Contributor Work): Define high-quality, user-centered discovery, activation, and monetization experiences across problem to success flows, upgrade flows, pricing surfaces, and lifecycle touchpoints — setting patterns that scale across the platform. Work from concept to production, delivering thoughtful UX, polished visual design, and vibe coded prototypes that help the organization understand direction, risk, and value. Use behavioral data as a primary design input: interpret funnel metrics, experiment results, and user signals to inform design decisions, not just validate them. Design and lead experiments across acquisition, activation, and expansion funnels — from hypothesis formation through read-out, in close partnership with product and data science. Establish reusable growth patterns in Mural's design system that balance clarity, persuasion, and long-term user trust. Partner with engineers to ensure accurate, high-quality implementation of flows and components. Coaching Responsibilities (Practice Leadership & Management): Directly manage one to three designers on the growth surface: run regular 1:1s, set goals, give performance feedback, and support their career growth. Balance IC output with people leadership — this is a hands-on management role, not a full-time management track. Expect the majority of your time to remain in design work. Model how to hold craft and commercial intent simultaneously — showing peers what it looks like to design for conversion without compromising user trust. Mentor designers working on growth-adjacent surfaces, developing their instincts around hierarchy, motivation, friction, and funnel thinking. Contribute to how the team understands growth design as a discipline: a principled approach to earning user commitment. Champion the relationship between growth quality and product quality, helping leadership understand when they align and when they're in tension. Partner with research, data science, and product to elevate experimentation quality across the organization. Hybrid Responsibilities (Both Player & Coach): Reframe problems at the funnel level helping teams understand where value is earned or lost and why. Lead workshops or working sessions that bring clarity to pricing, packaging, onboarding, and upgrade moment opportunities. Collaborate with product, research, and data science to define success metrics, shape experiment hypotheses, and interpret outcomes. Advocate for user trust as a growth asset, not an obstacle to conversion — and model how design holds that line. Design & Research Team Contribution: Share growth approaches for designing discovery, onboarding, and identity flows with peers through critique and collaboration. Partner with research, data, and product teams to elevate experimentation quality and improve how Mural understands user value signals. Contribute to a culture of design excellence, especially in areas where growth and monetization intersect with core product experiences. What you’ll bring 8+ years of product design experience, ideally in SaaS, productivity tools, collaboration software, or product-led growth environments. 2+ years of managing other designers A track record of leading growth, monetization, or conversion-focused design work — not just contributing to it. Deep fluency in funnel thinking: you understand acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion as a connected system, not isolated moments. Strong data instincts: you can read behavioral data, interpret experiment results, and use both to sharpen design decisions. Exceptional craft: visual clarity, spacing, motion, and interaction polish are second nature. Systems thinking: you understand how decisions cascade across surfaces, journeys, and user relationships over time. Experience mentoring or leading other designers, even informally — you know how to raise the quality of work around you. Strong communication skills that help cross-functional partners make smart, user-centered decisions. Comfort operating in spaces where patterns don’t yet exist and playbooks need to be written. Also great if you bring Experience with pricing architecture, packaging strategy, or monetization model design. Deep experience mapping and designing activation journeys — the full arc from first action to genuine value realization. Hands-on experience using AI-assisted tools and vibe coding to prototype growth flows, simulate behavioral nudges, and stress-test funnel logic in motion — treating code as a design material for rapid exploration. Background in organic acquisition or activation funnels at scale. Familiarity with AI-assisted experiences or contextual intelligence in growth flows. Experience working with data science teams on experimentation frameworks or causal inference. History of shaping 0→1 growth systems or redesigning broken acquisition or retention loops. Why you’ll love Mural You’ll help shape how millions of people discover value in Mural, understand what the product can do for them, and make confident choices about their journey. You’ll design experiences that balance business goals with user trust, clarity, and delight. You’ll collaborate with thoughtful partners who care about evidence, craft, and outcomes. At Mural, we “drink our own champagne” and use our product daily to collaborate, ideate, and prototype together. This role is Canada Remote. Your design work will shape how millions of people around the world collaborate. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Equal Opportunity We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

title: Account Executive, Enterprise Suite - Corporate
description: About AlphaSense : AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com . Come join us. About the Role AlphaSense is the market leader in AI driven search and due to client demand, AlphaSense is expanding our Enterprise Suite Sales Team to lead top-down sales into the largest global enterprises. Enterprise Suite securely enables clients to generate unique insights from a combined library of the client’s own qualitative intellectual property and AlphaSense’s trusted external content sets. This solution leverages AlphaSense’s market leading proprietary GenAI and LLM, to enable the client’s IP to be more discoverable and actionable. For further information, please visit https://www.alpha-sense.com/platform/enterprise/ Who You Are A proven top-down seller with experience selling complex technical solutions (APIs, AI/LLM platforms, data infrastructure, or enterprise software) into the largest global enterprises, at both the technical and C-suite level. Comfortable in technical conversations. You can discuss agentic architectures, MCP, authentication, security, and integration with developers and architects, and then connect it to business value for executive sponsors. Experienced selling into large corporates across industries such as technology, healthcare and life sciences, consumer and retail, energy and industrials, and professional services. A seller who owns the opportunity from start to finish, including a technical evaluation or proof of concept. ABOUT THE ROLE: The Product Support Manager will be responsible for leading a team of Product Support Specialists in Hyderabad. You will collaborate closely with the Hyderabad Site Lead, regional Heads of Support, and User Operations leadership to ensure cohesive product support operations across the global team. This role will surface customer and product usage trends, drive resolution for executive-level product escalations, and continuously improve global support and escalation processes. The successful candidate should bring deep expertise in product support and escalation management, including experience driving process improvements and collaborating cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success teams. They will also have strong experience managing a high-performing team of product support specialists across multiple levels, ensuring timely issue resolution, operational excellence, and a seamless customer experience. Own, coordinate and ship process improvements in collaboration with the User Ops, and influence on behalf of CX for cross-functionally owned processes and tools. - Participate in the global on-call rotation to cover incidents.
